faq.q: How is a titanium conflat knife-edge ring manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium conflat knife-edge ring is manufactured using Precision CNC turning; Electropolishing; Class 100 cleanroom cleaning; Helium leak testing. BOZE CNC Ti uses precision CNC equipment with strict process controls to ensure consistent quality and dimensional accuracy.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V for titanium conflat knife-edge ring?
faq.a: Alternative materials include stainless steel (heavier, susceptible to corrosion) and aluminum (lower strength, shorter fatigue life). The alternative manufacturing method is Manual turning on conventional lathes (less consistent, higher rejection rate).

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium conflat knife-edge ring?
faq.a: Titanium Conflat Knife-Edge Ring components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348, ASME. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium conflat knife-edge ring?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (ASTM F86). BOZE CNC Ti mitigates these through strict process control, proper material selection, and 100% inspection.
